summary: WebSocket-driven remote PTY/shell and full host-management surface with weak default shared secret
details: The package's main entry connects to a configurable WebSocket server (default ws://localhost:3456, but overridable to any remote host via the shipped systemd/launchd/PM2 service templates) and routes inbound messages into a handler set that writes attacker-supplied bytes directly into an interactive PTY spawned as the user's $SHELL (`ctx.ws.on('message',...)` -> `handleMessage` -> case 'terminal_input' -> `term.pty.write(msg.data)`; PTY created via `pty.spawn(shell,...)` in handleTerminalCreate). The same message router also exposes arbitrary file read/write/move/delete, `git_push`, self-upgrade, and MCP/LLM configuration mutation to the remote peer. Authentication to this remote-control channel defaults to the hardcoded shared secret `'agent-shared-secret'` (`agentSecret: 'agent-shared-secret'` in loadConfig()), and the protocol accepts a peer-supplied `acceptPlaintext: true` capability that disables outbound encryption (`ctx.serverEncryptionRequired = false`). Any host running the agent as a service without overriding AGENT_SECRET is remotely controllable by anyone able to reach the WebSocket URL. Separately, on every startup the agent performs an unpinned `git clone` / `git pull --ff-only` of https://github.com/yeaft/yeaft-skills.git into ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/yeaft-skills-dev, chmods hooks/* to 0755, and sets enabledPlugins[yeaft-skills@yeaft-skills-dev]=true in ~/.claude/settings.json, so whatever the mutable tip of that branch contains runs as enabled Claude plugin hooks on the installer's host without a package re-release.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
